title: FUNDIS Fungal Tissue Sampling for PCR
author: Harte Singer

steps.title: Prepare sampling workspace
steps.instruction: Find a hard, non‑porous surface that can be wiped clean with rubbing alcohol, turn off any fans and close windows to minimise air movement, wash your hands, and gather all materials and mushrooms for sampling.

steps.title: Set up PCR tube rack
steps.instruction: Place an empty PCR tube rack on the work surface, remove each strip of PCR tubes from its package with very clean hands, close the lids of each strip, and insert each strip into a row of the rack.

steps.title: Label PCR strips and tubes
steps.instruction: Using a Sharpie, label the hinges of each PCR strip as shown in the photo, label the first tube of each strip from 1‑12 top‑to‑bottom, and optionally label the last tube of each strip with the plate number (e.g., plate 5 → label the last tube on the right of each strip with “5”).

steps.title: Prepare tweezers
steps.instruction: Dip the tweezers into alcohol, wipe them thoroughly with a small piece of a clean Kimwipe, repeat until confident the tweezers are clean, then set the tweezers down so the tines do not touch any surface while you handle the mushroom.

steps.title: Remove first tube strip for sampling
steps.instruction: Remove the lid from the tube rack, take the first strip of 8 tubes, place it in a second rack for sampling; the first tube on the left will have “1” written on it and the first hinge will already be marked.

steps.title: Record specimen information
steps.instruction: Grab the box or bag containing the mushrooms, enter the accession number into the first cell of the data‑entry sheet, and write the tube number on the back of the voucher slip (e.g., 1‑1, 1‑2 … 12‑8).

steps.title: Collect tissue sample
steps.instruction: Open the mushroom container, either reach in with the tweezers or place the mushroom on a clean surface away from the tubes, and carefully cut a ~1 × 1 mm piece of clean tissue (hymenium tissue such as gill, pore, gleba, or apothecia is preferred). Avoid dirt, plant matter, or excess tissue; perform this step away from the tube rack to minimise cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to tube
steps.instruction: Place the tissue into the open tube and release it (or gently tap/wipe the tines inside the tube), then remove the tweezers, set them aside for cleaning, and close the tube cap. Be aware that static electricity can cause samples to stick to tube walls.

steps.title: Clean tweezers and repeat
steps.instruction: Clean the tweezers as described earlier and proceed with the next specimen, repeating steps 4‑8 for each mushroom.

steps.title: Return completed strip
steps.instruction: After all 8 tubes of the strip are filled, place the completed strip back into its original row in the tube rack and remove the next strip of tubes for sampling.

steps.title: Seal and label rack
steps.instruction: Place the plastic cover on the tube rack, tape the lid shut with lab tape or masking tape, and label the base of the rack and the lid with lab tape or masking tape.

steps.title: Sample tissue by mushroom type
steps.instruction: Collect tissue according to the morphology of the specimen:

substeps.instruction: Gilled mushrooms – sample a very small piece of the gill.
Mushrooms with pores – sample a very small piece of pore tissue.
Cup fungi – sample from the inner surface of the cup (the side facing away from the substrate); include the stalk if present.
Inverted cup fungi – sample from the exterior tissue on the end of the stalk.
Truffles – sample from the interior; usually slice the truffle in half and take one or more interior pieces.
Puffballs – sample the soft, often powdery interior while avoiding release of spores; handle these specimens last to prevent cross‑contamination and avoid breathing spores.
Crusts – sample any part of the flat fruiting body, avoiding digging into the substrate; if the surface is completely flat, scrape a bit of material with tweezers.
Bird's nests – break apart a peridiole (the “egg” inside) and sample that material.

steps.title: Package rack for shipping
steps.instruction: Pack the tube rack in a box with plenty of padding to ensure optimal shipping conditions.
